clue.text: Pat's so rich it makes one tense

indicators.note: the letters of the first four words are made into something new, a rearranged phrase

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A remark that Pat's great wealth puts somebody on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is the anagram signal working on PATS SO RICH IT; 'tense' looks like an adjective meaning nervous but is the grammatical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a French past tense used in formal writing, so it is one grammatical tense.

clue.text: A lettered chap after a job

definitions.text: A lettered chap after a job

parts.words: A lettered chap after a job
parts.note: a man who carries letters, read as a man whose work is the post; 'lettered' pretends to mean learned

explanation.surface: An educated man is looking for employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lettered' usually means well read; here it means carrying letters, and the job he does is delivering the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier is a man who handles letters for a living, the job being the delivery round.

clue.text: Cross reference to the cause of rising damp

definitions.meaning: a note telling the reader to look at another page
water slowly leaking up through a wall or floor

explanation.surface: An instruction pointing a reader to where the damp problem is explained.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a book's pointer to another page; as one word it is slow leakage of water through masonry.

clue.text: What the impoverished admirer of Dickens may fall upon

definitions.text: What the impoverished admirer of Dickens may fall upon

parts.words: What the impoverished admirer of Dickens may fall upon
parts.note: the idiom for becoming poor, to fall upon difficult days, is also the title of a Dickens novel a fan would seize on

explanation.surface: A poor fan of Dickens has something to fall back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall upon' works twice: the poor fall upon difficult days, and a Dickens lover falls eagerly upon his 1854 novel of that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a period of poverty and is also a Dickens novel, fitting both halves of the picture.

clue.text: Refuse to fight

definitions.meaning: a noun here: waste or leftover bits thrown away

explanation.surface: Declining to take part in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both leftover waste material and a minor brawl.

clue.text: Chris to get disentangled from a bird

indicators.note: the letters of the name and 'to' are untangled and laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Chris has to free himself from a bird's clutches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get disentangled' is the anagram signal on CHRIS and TO; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless African species is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Copy one friend imbibing sweet vermouth

indicators.note: drinking in, so the friend takes the vermouth inside

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, sweet vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A drinker apes a pal who is sipping sweet vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' signals the container. 'It' for Italian sweet vermouth comes from the British bar order 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to mimic or ape them.

clue.text: Game fellow takes ship around the harbour with its captain

indicators.note: the ship's letters are placed round the harbour

parts.note: a ship's master is its captain

explanation.surface: A sporty man takes a vessel round the harbour with the skipper aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container. A sports master is a British school's games teacher, hence 'Game fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The schoolteacher in charge of games and athletics is a man of sport.

clue.text: His bacteriological research affected over half of Europe

indicators.note: the first three of the six letters of the continent's name

explanation.surface: A scientist's germ studies changed things across much of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the first three letters of EUROPE. The definition is the French scientist whose research gave milk 'pasteurised'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French chemist Louis's germ research led to the heat treatment of milk named after him.

clue.text: Hamelin's treacherous response to the Pied Piper's calling

definitions.text: Hamelin's treacherous response to the Pied Piper's calling

parts.words: Hamelin's treacherous response to the Pied Piper's calling
parts.note: the town broke its promise to pay, betraying him, and his calling was catching vermin

explanation.surface: Hamelin's betrayal of the piper who cleared its streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both betraying (the town refused to pay the Piper) and catching rodents, the Piper's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to betray them, and the same word names the trade of catching vermin.

clue.text: Animal Vegetable Mineral? That is matter of conjecture

definitions.meaning: a parlour quiz where players narrow down a hidden object by asking yes/no questions
any business of speculating or estimating

explanation.surface: A parlour game whose whole point is speculation.
explanation.walkthrough: Animal, Vegetable or Mineral is a British radio and parlour quiz of twenty yes/no questions.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiz is a pastime of inferring a hidden object, and figuratively any situation decided by speculation.

clue.text: Batter section which is defending the fort

explanation.surface: A segment of the wall being pounded while the fort is held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' looks like a cook's mixture or a cricketer but is the verb to ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad defensive earth wall around a castle protects the stronghold.

clue.text: Tommy is not in the public eye

definitions.meaning: a Tommy is a British ordinary soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier who keeps a low profile.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy, or Tommy Atkins, is the old British nickname for a soldier of the lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest army rank is this soldier, and the adjective means kept away from public view.

clue.text: It explains why evil is pursued by the Anglican church

indicators.note: followed, so the church comes after the evil

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Wickedness is chased by the Church of England, which is why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is pursued by' signals that the church comes last; 'It explains why' is the definition, a word giving a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means 'because', introducing the reason for something.

clue.text: Has no peer got anything to light a cigarette with?

definitions.text: got anything to light a cigarette with?
definitions.meaning: lacking matches, the means of lighting up

explanation.surface: A smoker asks a lord whether he has a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests a lord; it is an equal. Split, the word reads as 'match-less', short of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Without equal is unrivalled, and split as two parts it means having no matches to strike.

clue.text: Theodore Roosevelt? Pooh!

definitions.meaning: the toy was named after the president, nicknamed Teddy, who spared a bear cub
Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear of A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the mention of a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pooh!' looks like an exclamation of scorn but names Milne's toy bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The stuffed toy took the president's nickname, and Milne's Pooh is such a soft toy.

clue.text: Di appears to be in disarray when given the once over

indicators.note: the letters of the name and the verb are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Di looks a mess when somebody looks her up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in disarray' is the anagram signal on DI APPEARS; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess or evaluate is to look something over quickly and judge it.

clue.text: Board one first writes on

explanation.surface: A notice board is the first thing someone writes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the numeral ahead of 'on'. 'Board' is lodging with meals, as in full board, not a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarding house on the Continent offers lodging and meals, the same sense as board and lodging.

clue.text: A pine-fruit containing it is poisonous

definitions.note: an adjective in the clue, defining a poisonous plant, a noun

indicators.note: holding inside, so the cone wraps round 'it'

parts.note: a pine's fruit is its cone

explanation.surface: A pine cone with something inside that is toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' signals the container. The plant, monkshood or wolfsbane, is highly toxic; the printed (5,2) count is wrong for this one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood is a deadly toxic plant, so the definition describes it by its venom.

clue.text: Assumed to back in bed

indicators.note: the phrase for being in bed is read from its end

explanation.surface: Presumed to be lying back in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NOT UP round.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a manner or garment is to don it, as in feigning an accent.

clue.text: Open row develops when electricity is available

indicators.note: the two words grow into a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out once the lights come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' is the anagram signal on OPEN ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the state of a switched-on supply, when current flows.

clue.text: An order likely to prickle

definitions.meaning: the Order of the ..., Scotland's highest chivalric honour

explanation.surface: An instruction that is bound to irritate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command; it is the Scottish order of knighthood named after this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's chivalric Order bears this plant's name, and the plant itself is covered in spines.

clue.text: A number of fellows reveal muscular features

explanation.surface: Several men show off their muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow or tutor at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The cords joining muscle to bone are parts of the muscular system.

clue.text: A line in a letter backfires

indicators.note: the word 'fires' is written with its letters in the opposite order

parts.note: the second half of 'backfires' read as its own word; that its reversal also sits inside the whole printed word is a coincidence of the split

explanation.surface: A stroke of the pen in a letter goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfires' splits into 'back' (the reversal signal) and 'fires'. A letter here is a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: The small finishing stroke on a typeface's character is a short line.

clue.text: Gaping open-mouthed

definitions.meaning: with jaws stretched wide, as when tired

explanation.surface: Gawping with a dropped jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide chasm is described this way, and so is a tired person stretching their jaws.

clue.text: It's not so fine being a Mediterranean prince

explanation.surface: Being a Monaco royal is not so wonderful after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as excellent but is weather; Monaco's Prince Rainier III married Grace Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetter weather is less fair, and Monaco's ruler from 1949 bore the name.

clue.text: Rum rate review calls for correction

indicators.note: the two words are looked at again and their letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A reviewer's odd verdict on a poor rating needs putting right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' is the anagram signal on RUM RATE; 'calls for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed slip listing a book's mistakes is an amendment or fix.

clue.text: Meddling in renovation of free centre

indicators.note: the words are rebuilt, their letters made over into a new form

explanation.surface: Interfering with the refurbishment of a free community centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renovation of' is the anagram signal on IN FREE CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking one's nose into others' affairs is intrusion.
